issues.name: user-intelligence (new repo) - embedded inbound message capture for SMS/email/web
issues.description:
Build a new standalone repository at /home/fidika/user-intelligence as an embedded Go library, separate from authkit. The library receives inbound SMS/email webhooks plus generic web POST submissions, normalizes payloads, and stores them in Postgres for downstream intelligence workflows.

Scope and policy:
- Separate concern: keep this fully out of authkit.
- Embedded model: host applications mount library-provided routes and pass credentials/dependencies.
- Router agnostic requirement: expose standard net/http handlers so Gin, chi, stdlib mux, etc. can mount without adapter-specific APIs.
- MVP is ingestion plus persistence only; no auto-reply agent behavior.
- Provider scope for MVP: Twilio only for both SMS and email inbound routes.
- Auditability-first with a minimal schema: keep only the fields needed for routing, identity association, security_class, and conversation context.
- Trust boundaries: webhook routes are only for SMS/email provider callbacks with signature verification; web message route is a normal host POST route, not a webhook route.
- Twilio signature verification/parsing is performed inside library webhook handlers.
- Doujins mount convention: /api/v1/messages (web POST), /api/v1/messages/sms (Twilio SMS webhook), /api/v1/messages/email (Twilio email webhook).
- Web route identity source: read user_id directly from request context when available; anonymous web POSTs are allowed and create no participant link.
- Message security classification: mark source_channel trust as security_class=secure for Discord and direct web POST; mark SMS/email as security_class=insecure.
- Idempotent writes are required in MVP.
- Identity linking policy: always attempt to resolve user_id from sender identity (email/phone/discord) on ingest where applicable; when matched, attach user as a conversation participant; if no match is found, create no participant link.

issues.name: discord integration - ingest @mentions and DMs, reply on source channel
issues.description:
Add Discord as an inbound/outbound channel integrated with user-intelligence. Users should be able to message our Discord bot directly via DM, or mention us in servers where the bot exists (for example @doujins). Inbound events should be routed into user-intelligence ingestion and persisted with full Discord source metadata so replies can be sent back to the same channel/thread.

Scope and policy:
- Inbound source for DM/mention messages is Discord Gateway events over WebSocket (not Discord message webhooks).
- Runtime model: no separate machine/process; the Discord bot runtime is embedded in-process when user-intelligence is mounted in doujins.
- Use a bot account only; no self-bot behavior.
- Reply routing must target the channel the user used: DM replies to the DM channel, mention replies to the originating server channel/thread.
- Security classification: Discord inbound messages are security_class=secure even when no local authkit user is linked.
- Identity linking: resolve discord_user_id -> user_id via authkit/profiles provider links (profiles.user_providers where provider_slug='discord' and subject=<discord_user_id>) where available; if no match, keep no participant link (still accepted as secure Discord message).
- Respect Discord platform policy and anti-spam requirements (no unsolicited mass DMs, explicit user intent only).
- Persist channel metadata needed for deterministic replies: guild_id, channel_id, thread_id, message_id, author_id.
- Cluster policy: exactly one active owner per shard; shard 0 must always be active to receive DMs.

[x] Add canonical Discord metadata shape to persisted message records: guild_id, channel_id, thread_id, message_id, author_id, mention_target.
[x] Implement embedded Discord runtime/service (in-process) that connects to Gateway and receives MESSAGE_CREATE events.

[x] Implement shard manager for clustered doujins with lease-based shard ownership so only one node owns each shard.
[x] Ensure shard 0 ownership is always maintained in-cluster so DM events are continuously received.
[x] Implement Gateway session lifecycle: heartbeat, resume, identify, invalid-session handling, reconnect with jittered backoff.

[x] Implement inbound filters: accept direct messages to bot and server messages that mention @doujins; ignore unrelated chatter.

issues.name: conversation threading model - context-aware back-and-forth storage
issues.description:
Add first-class conversation/thread storage so messages are grouped into durable conversational context instead of isolated events. This conversation system is required baseline in the database before rollout.

Minimal modeling goals:
- Use three core tables: conversations, messages, and conversation_participants.
- Every message (sms/email/discord/web, inbound/outbound) must belong to a conversation.
- Keep user association at conversation level; do not duplicate user_id on messages.
- Use one source_channel field; do not split into separate channel/provider fields.
- Keep only fields required for routing, security_class, and context retrieval.
- Use deterministic conversation_key per source_channel so inbound messages consistently attach to the same thread.
- Store minimal per-message source_context needed for routing replies and threading.
tasks: [x] Define Postgres schema migration for user_intelligence.conversations with minimal columns: id (uuid pk), source_channel, conversation_key, last_message_at, created_at.

[x] Define Postgres schema migration for user_intelligence.conversation_participants with minimal columns: conversation_id uuid not null references conversations(id), user_id uuid not null, created_at; primary key (conversation_id, user_id).

[x] Define Postgres schema migration for user_intelligence.messages with minimal columns: id (uuid pk), conversation_id uuid not null references conversations(id), source_channel, direction (inbound|outbound), source_identity, source_context jsonb, security_class (secure|insecure), body_text, provider_message_id nullable, created_at.
[x] Enforce DB integrity rules so no message can exist outside a conversation: NOT NULL conversation_id + FK + test coverage.

[x] Add essential indexes only: unique conversations(source_channel, conversation_key), conversations(source_channel, last_message_at desc), conversation_participants(user_id, conversation_id), messages(conversation_id, created_at), and messages(provider_message_id) where provider_message_id is not null.

[x] Define per-channel conversation association rules with deterministic conversation_key derivation (sms/email/discord/web) so inbound messages always map to existing conversation or create exactly one new conversation.
[x] Implement transactional create-or-attach conversation write path so conversation selection/creation and message insert happen atomically.
[x] Implement outbound persistence so replies are always stored in the same conversation_id.
[x] Add read helpers: list conversations for a user (via conversation_participants) and fetch last N messages in a conversation for context.
[x] Add tests for per-channel association, multi-user participant linking, conversation continuation, and hard failure when inserting message rows without conversation_id.
[x] Define minimal source_context schema by source_channel (discord ids, sms from/to, email thread ids, web thread token) for reply routing and thread continuation.

issues.name: Responses API-native orchestration - update_memory, send, create_issue
issues.description:
Plan and implement the core AI execution flow for inbound messages using OpenAI Responses API semantics directly so the library mirrors API naming and data shapes as closely as possible.

Responses API contract:
- Host passes OpenAI API key/config to the library.
- Library owns and initializes the OpenAI Responses client internally.
- Library request payload mirrors Responses fields: `model`, `input`, `tools`, `previous_response_id`, and optional `metadata`.
- Tool definitions mirror Responses function tools: `type=function`, `name`, `description`, `parameters` (JSON Schema), `strict=true`.
- Tool execution consumes `response.output` items with `type=function_call` (`call_id`, `name`, `arguments`) and returns `input` items with `type=function_call_output` (`call_id`, `output`).
- Loop continues by calling Responses again with `previous_response_id` until final assistant content is produced or stop conditions fire.

Delivery contract:
- Library-built Twilio sender handles `send` for twilio_sms and twilio_email using host-provided Twilio config.
- Web delivery is intrinsic to the mounted web route: the route streams responses over SSE directly (no web sender implementation).

Tool set:
- update_memory: update per-user memory blob with newly learned information.
- send: send a reply back in the same source_channel/conversation for provider-delivered channels.
- create_issue: create/update a human-triage queue item with dedupe so repeated reports map to one canonical issue.

Issue queue requirement:
- Keep a single issues table in user_intelligence for human triage.
- If multiple users report the same bug, keep one canonical issue row (deduped by normalized hash) and update report_count/last_seen_at instead of inserting duplicates.

Web UX requirement:
- For web source_channel, stream Responses-style events to frontend over SSE in the same request lifecycle.
tasks: [x] Define end-to-end processing pipeline: inbound message -> conversation association -> participant linking -> Responses API loop -> persisted tool effects/outbound artifacts.
[x] Define minimal host config surface: OpenAI config (api_key required; model defaultable; optional base_url/timeout) plus Twilio config for SMS/email sending.
[x] Define canonical Responses request shape used internally: `model`, `input`, `tools`, `previous_response_id`, optional `metadata`.
[x] Define exact function tool specs for `update_memory`, `send`, and `create_issue` using Responses field names (`type=function`, `name`, `description`, `parameters`, `strict=true`).
[x] Define strict JSON Schemas for `update_memory`, `send`, and `create_issue` arguments and validate before handler execution.
[x] Implement built-in OpenAI Responses client integration in library with parity to Responses request/response field naming.
[x] Implement tool registry: function name -> Go handler, arg validator, and serialized `function_call_output` result encoder.

[x] Implement Responses loop mechanics: create initial response, parse `response.output` items, execute each `function_call`, submit follow-up `input` with `function_call_output`, set `previous_response_id`, repeat until final output or max steps.
[x] Implement loop safeguards aligned to Responses flow: reject unknown function names, reject invalid arguments, cap function-call count, detect no-progress loops, and fail closed.

[x] Persist orchestration trace fields keyed to Responses objects: `response.id`, `previous_response_id`, `output` item ids/types, `function_call.call_id`, function name, execution status, and error payloads.
[x] Define Postgres migration for user_intelligence.user_memory (minimal): id, user_id, memory_blob, updated_at.

[x] Define Postgres migration for user_intelligence.agent_issues queue (minimal): id, conversation_id, source_channel, issue_type, title, body, dedupe_hash, status(open|closed), report_count, first_seen_at, last_seen_at, created_at.
[x] Define unique dedupe constraint for agent_issues (for example on dedupe_hash + open status) to prevent duplicate triage entries.
[x] Implement update_memory handler: atomic upsert by user_id with merge/replace strategy and audit metadata.
[x] Implement create_issue handler: insert queue item when new; on dedupe hit update existing row (report_count++, last_seen_at, optional freshest context fields) and return existing issue reference.
[x] Implement send handler for provider-delivered channels (twilio_sms/twilio_email) and persist outbound message in same conversation_id.
[x] Keep OpenAI config surface minimal in library; require api_key, allow model override, and default sane timeout/token limits.
[x] Implement message-level idempotency guard so the same inbound message does not trigger duplicate Responses/tool execution.

[x] Enforce per-conversation serialized processing for the Responses/tool pipeline (for example DB advisory lock by conversation_id) so concurrent inbound messages do not race and corrupt context ordering.
[x] Implement mounted web route SSE response path as thin pass-through of Responses-style event semantics (including text deltas and completion/failure) with minimal additional wrapping.
[x] Implement non-web channel mode: async processing with persisted outbound response and provider send status updates.
[x] Add deterministic smoke test: inbound 'ping' should produce 'pong' in the same source_channel and same conversation.
[x] Add tests for each tool path (update_memory/send/create_issue), issue dedupe behavior, and SSE streaming contract.
[x] Add tests for Responses loop behavior: function-call chain, `previous_response_id` chaining, `function_call_output` handling, invalid args, unknown function, and loop-cap termination.
[x] Add operational controls: feature flags per source_channel, kill switch, execution timeout, and basic safety guardrails.
[x] Implement built-in Twilio sender module (SMS + email) in library, including auth setup, sender identity config, and provider error normalization.

issues.name: minimal AI reply agent - respond in same channel and conversation
issues.description:
Add a minimal AI reply agent that can read recent conversation context and send replies back through the same source_channel the user used (web, twilio_sms, twilio_email, discord). Keep this intentionally small and safe for MVP: deterministic behavior, basic guardrails, and clear observability.

Minimal scope:
- Trigger on eligible inbound messages and create one outbound reply message.
- Reply in the same conversation_id and source_channel.
- Start with a simple smoke behavior (ping -> pong) plus a basic LLM reply path behind feature flags.
tasks: [x] Define agent runtime boundaries: asynchronous worker, no blocking in webhook/request handlers, and one processing pass per inbound message.
[x] Add minimal agent config: enabled flag, model id, max context messages, max output chars, and per-source_channel enable flags.
[x] Implement eligibility filter for inbound messages (ignore system/internal messages; optional allowlist while rolling out).
[x] Implement deterministic smoke test behavior: when inbound body_text is exactly 'ping' (case-insensitive), produce 'pong'.
[x] Implement context loader: fetch last N messages by conversation_id for prompt context.
[x] Implement minimal prompt template using conversation context and source_channel metadata.
[x] Implement reply generation path (LLM call) guarded by feature flag; fallback to no-op if disabled or provider unavailable.
[x] Implement outbound router by source_channel: web response path, Twilio SMS send, Twilio email send, Discord send.
[x] Persist outbound reply into messages table with direction=outbound in the same conversation_id.
[x] Add idempotent processing key so the same inbound message is not replied to twice.
[x] Add basic safety controls: max reply length, timeout, and denylist for sensitive actions.
[x] Add metrics and logs: reply_attempted_total, reply_sent_total, reply_failed_total, reply_latency_ms.
[x] Add tests for ping->pong across source_channel routes, single-reply idempotency, and conversation linkage correctness.
[x] Add a rollout plan: dev-only enablement, canary by source_channel, and fast kill switch.
